Under Regulation F, a debt collector must not call repeatedly or continuously with intent to annoy, abuse, or harass [R-1006.14#1]. A collector is presumed to violate this rule if it calls you about a particular debt more than seven times within seven consecutive days, or calls within seven days after a telephone conversation with you about that debt [R-1006.14#1]. Some calls, such as those not connected to the dialed number or those placed with your prior consent, don't count toward those limits [R-1006.14#1].

A collector also must not contact you at a time or place it knows or should know is inconvenient. Unless it knows otherwise, before 8:00 a.m. or after 9:00 p.m. your local time is inconvenient [R-1006.6#1]. It must not contact you at work if it knows or has reason to know your employer prohibits such communication [R-1006.6#1]. If you notify a collector in writing that you want it to stop communicating with you, it generally must stop contacting you about that debt, with limited exceptions [R-1006.6#1].

Next steps: we will review your complaint, including call dates and times and when you told the collector about your employer's policy. Please send any call logs or screenshots you have. We cannot promise a particular outcome, but we will review the facts against these rules.
